pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: mac80211: mac80211: Check SN for deactivated mpaths When processing a PREQ or PREP it's critical to use the incoming SN. If that is improperly done routing loops and other types of badness can happen. But the code was always processing path messages for deactivated paths. This path fixes that so that if we have a valid SN then we use it to verify that it is a message we can accept. For reference the relevant section of the standard is 13.10.8.4 which doesn't address the deactivated path case at all. I also included a special case for when our peer reboots or restarts networking. This is an important case because without it there can be a very long delay before we accept path messages from that peer. It's also a simple case and intimately associated with processing messages for deactivated paths so I used one patch instead of two. (cherry picked from commit "d8f0300a7aca5cd9208112104c64d894ad82da1f") (source: git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/ath.git) BUG=chrome-os-partner:49352 TEST=build/boot on Arkham and verified iperf throughput. Signed-off-by: Alexis Green <agreen@cococorp.com> Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/322375 Commit-Ready: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Peter Oh <poh@qca.qualcomm.com> Tested-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Change-Id: I55dde29a634e899c37641379da7cc35aa489e4cb Signed-off-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340249 Commit-Ready: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: mac80211: mesh: fix call_rcu() usage When using call_rcu(), the called function may be delayed quite significantly, and without a matching rcu_barrier() there's no way to be sure it has finished. Therefore, global state that could be gone/freed/reused should never be touched in the callback. Fix this in mesh by moving the atomic_dec() into the caller; that's not really a problem since we already unlinked the path and it will be destroyed anyway. This fixes a crash Jouni observed when running certain tests in a certain order, in which the mesh interface was torn down, the memory reused for a function pointer (work struct) and running that then crashed since the pointer had been decremented by 1, resulting in an invalid instruction byte stream. (cherry picked from commit "c2e703a55245bfff3db53b1f7cbe59f1ee8a4339") (source: git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/ath.git) BUG=chrome-os-partner:49352 TEST=build/boot on Arkham and verified iperf throughput. CHROMIUM: mac80211: mesh airtime link metric fixes Airtime link metric value is a function of bit rate (in kbps) and paket error rate, and good estimates of them are important to derive meaningful metric and to attain desirable routing decisions. This CL aims to improve exisiting implementation which uses instantaneous bitrate value and does not account for retries when calculating packet error rate. It maintains a exponential moving average for bitrate, and the weight is tunable from debugfs. It also includes retry count for the purpose of calculating packet error rate. For example, if a packet is tried 3 times and the 4th attempt succeeds, then the packet error rate is 0.75. BUG=b:26546424 TEST=manually on 4 WWs and 1 AK forming a mesh Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/322773 Commit-Ready: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Tested-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Change-Id: I034522334880b84b7e44055a08f404735a8e6c38 Signed-off-by: Julan Hsu <julanhsu@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340402 Commit-Ready: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: mac80211: support device/driver PN check for CCMP/GCMP When there are multiple RX queues, the PN checks in mac80211 cannot be used since packets might be processed out of order on different CPUs. Allow the driver to report that the PN has been checked, drivers that will use multi-queue RX will have to set this flag. For now, the flag is only valid when the frame has been decrypted, in theory that restriction doesn't have to be there, but in practice the hardware will have decrypted the frame already. overlays: move TTY_CONSOLE to make.defaults TTY_CONSOLE is an incremental variable in our portage profile (see USE_EXPAND). We have previously hacked around this, because portage didn't always handle it properly, but now that portage is fixed up, we should be handling it in make.defaults (which can stack properly) instead of in make.conf (which typically clobbers any existing definition). This theoretically makes the X vs. freon selection work a little nicer, even if we might not care practically any more. By inspection, this shouldn't cause any noticeable changes because: (a) most of these TTY_CONSOLE definitions are comment out anyway; (b) for those that aren't, they either (i) didn't try to (incorrectly) do incremental assignments anyway or (ii) don't appear to use freon (I only checked the top-level overlay; I didn't check all the parent structure). (IOW, I don't believe any of these overlays actually exhibit the issue in http://crbug.com/606100 -- but this still qualifies as cleanup.) BUG=chromium:606100 TEST=`emerge-${BOARD} -av chromeos-base/tty` and check the value of TTY_CONSOLE; also check for /etc/init/console-tty*.conf; I did this test for several boards, and only inspected the remaining Change-Id: If7573ad6de9f0d09818fbd1ded3e19f0a031697c Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340902 Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>
